formation.title: SPQR: Senatus Populusque Romanus
formation.text:
It is done. What centuries of ambition, blood, and devotion have labored toward is now manifest: the Roman Empire stands reborn. The ancient seat of the Caesars at Rome is ours. The walls of Constantinople bow to our standard. From the forums where Cicero spoke to the harbors where the grain ships once sailed, this dominion spans the known world.

The Senate and People of Rome (those ancient words, half-forgotten in the long darkness since the fall) ring out again through marble halls. Scholars weep. Soldiers kneel before the eagles. The common folk whisper that the prophecy has been fulfilled: Rome is eternal.

But a restored empire must choose its soul. The old Romans knew two paths to greatness, and the question that divided Caesar from Augustus, Trajan from Hadrian, now falls to us. Shall Rome rule through the irresistible force of its legions, imposing universal order through strength? Or shall Rome rule through the irresistible force of its civilization, making all peoples wish to call themselves Roman?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: The eagles shall darken every horizon.

modifiers.name: Imperium Romanum Restitutum
modifiers.text: The Roman Empire has been restored not as an idea, but as a reality of steel and law. From the seven hills of Rome, the eagles fly once more over a dominion that stretches from ocean to ocean. The legions march again (disciplined, relentless, irresistible) and the world remembers what it means to defy Rome. Universal law binds every province to the center, and the authority of the Imperator brooks no dissent.

options.text: Let the light of Rome illuminate every land.

modifiers.name: Lux Aeterna
modifiers.text: Rome endures not because of her legions, but because of what she represents. To be Roman is to be civilized: to know law, to value learning, to build roads and aqueducts that outlast the ages. This restored empire does not merely conquer; it transforms. Every people it touches is given the gift of Roman civilization, and in return, Rome absorbs what is best in them. The eternal light of the Caput Mundi illuminates the world.

destiny.name: SPQR Restored
destiny.text: The Roman Empire stands reborn. Stabilize the realm and choose the path that will define this new Rome for the ages.

event.title: The Senate Convenes
event.text: For the first time in over a thousand years, the Roman Senate convenes in its ancient chamber. The marble halls echo with deliberation as senators, drawn from every corner of this reborn empire, debate the future of Rome. The eagles have been raised. The question now is not whether Rome endures, but how it shall endure.

destiny.name: Pax Romana Imposita
destiny.text: Rome's peace is not given: it is imposed. Extend the eagles beyond the old frontiers. The holy cities of Arabia and the Germanic Rhine must bow to Roman authority.

event.title: Pax Romana Imposita
event.text: The legions have crossed frontiers that even Trajan only dreamed of. The holy cities of Arabia have fallen. The Germanic tribes beyond the Rhine, those eternal thorns in Rome's side, have at last been brought to heel. Roman forts now stand where no Roman eagle has flown before. The first phase of the new conquest is complete, and the world takes notice: this is not a ceremonial restoration. This is Rome as it was always meant to be.

options.text: The eagles fly where they will.

destiny.name: Limes Ultimus
destiny.text: The old limes were a line of retreat. The new limes are a line of advance. Push the frontier to the heart of Russia and the highlands of Persia. Let the world know there is no land Rome cannot reach.

conditions.text: Own Moscow, or a subject owns it
Own Esfahân, or a subject owns it

event.title: Beyond the Old Frontiers
event.text:
The legions have achieved what no Roman army has done before. Moscow and Isfahan (cities that the ancient Romans never saw, never even imagined) now fly the Roman standard. The frontier stretches from the frozen forests of Russia to the sun-baked plateaus of Persia.

But such an empire demands a choice about how its soldiers are organized. Shall we maintain the old Roman tradition of a small, supremely disciplined professional army? Or shall we embrace the reality of our vast frontiers and expand the limitanei, the border garrison system, to defend every mile of the limes?

options.text: Quality over quantity. Train the finest.

modifiers.name: Praetorian Discipline
modifiers.text: Rome's armies are trained to a standard of perfection that the ancient Praetorian Guard would envy. Fewer in number but unmatched in skill, these soldiers hold the frontiers through sheer professional excellence.

modifiers.name: Limitanei Expansion
modifiers.text: The frontier garrison system has been massively expanded. Every mile of the limes is defended by settled soldier-farmers who know their territory intimately. Separatism withers where the legions stand watch.

destiny.name: Orbis Terrarum
destiny.text: The inhabited world, the orbis terrarum, is Rome. From the green hills of Ireland to the bazaars of Samarkand, from the forests of Novgorod to the deserts of Arabia, no corner of the earth lies beyond the reach of the legions.

conditions.text: Own Samarkand, or a subject owns it
Own Dublin, or a subject owns it
Own Novgorod, or a subject owns it

event.title: The World is Rome
event.text:
It is done. From the green hills of Ireland to the ancient crossroads of Samarkand, from the frozen rivers of Novgorod to the burning sands of Arabia: all roads lead to Rome. The orbis terrarum, the circle of the known world, is Roman.

Philosophers debate whether this unprecedented dominion should be used to enforce a permanent peace, or whether Rome's nature demands eternal expansion. The legions await their orders.

modifiers.name: Pax Imperialis
modifiers.text: The peace of Rome is absolute. No nation dares challenge an empire that stretches across the known world. Roman subjects are loyal because they know no alternative, and Rome's overwhelming strength makes resistance futile.

options.text: Rome's hunger can never be sated.

modifiers.name: Bellum Perpetuum
modifiers.text: Rome is a machine of conquest that cannot be stopped. War feeds the treasury through plunder, and the treasury funds more war. The cycle is self-sustaining, though the constant campaigns drive prices ever upward.

destiny.name: Renovatio Studii
destiny.text: A renewal of learning. Rome's silk trade funds a new golden age of scholarship, and a library in Rome itself gathers the books of the world. The wealth of civilization, not the sword, will bind the world to Rome.

A market the country is in

Silk is traded in the market

event.title: Renovatio Studii
event.text: A new golden age of learning dawns. Roman merchants fund the construction of great libraries and academies across the empire. Scholars from every province (Greek philosophers, Egyptian mathematicians, Persian astronomers) gather in Rome to share their knowledge. The silk that flows through Roman markets pays for manuscripts that will outlast empires. This is Rome's true gift to the world: not the sword, but the book.

options.text: Let knowledge be our greatest conquest.

destiny.name: Mare Nostrum Mercator
destiny.text: The Mediterranean is truly 'our sea' once more: not as a Roman lake of warships, but as the greatest market the world has ever known. Alexandria, the emporium of the East, and Carthage, the second city of the Latin West, are built up into the harbours they were under the Caesars. Roman books spread knowledge as Roman ships spread goods.

conditions.text: We own Alexandria and its development is at least 59
We own Tunis, the site of Carthage, and its development is at least 47

event.title: The Roman Market
event.text:
The Mediterranean, Mare Nostrum, hums with commerce as it has not done since the height of the old empire. Roman trade routes stretch from the Atlantic to the Indian Ocean. Roman books carry Roman law, Roman knowledge, and Roman prices to every corner of the known world.

This unprecedented prosperity raises a question: shall Rome invest in its scholars and universities, building the most learned civilization the world has ever seen? Or shall it codify its commercial law, making Roman markets the standard against which all others are measured?

modifiers.name: Collegium Doctorum
modifiers.text: The great colleges of Rome are the envy of the world. Scholars from every nation seek admission, and the knowledge they produce drives unprecedented prosperity. The cost of maintaining these institutions means less coin for the legions.

modifiers.name: Lex Mercatoria
modifiers.text: Roman commercial law, the Lex Mercatoria, is the standard by which all trade is conducted. Roman merchants enjoy unmatched advantages in every market, and Roman trade centers dominate the economic landscape.

destiny.name: Caput Mundi
destiny.text: The Head of the World. Rome is not merely a city or even an empire: it is the fountainhead of civilization itself. The town that shrank among its ruins is built up to twice what it was. The new sciences flow from Roman academies. Every nation measures itself against the Roman standard.

conditions.text: We own Rome and its development is at least 63

event.title: Caput Mundi
event.text:
Rome is the head of the world: not through conquest, but through the irresistible force of civilization. The new sciences that reshape the world flow from Roman academies. Every nation that wishes to be called civilized adopts Roman institutions, Roman law, Roman standards of learning.

This civilizational supremacy offers Rome a final choice. Shall it embrace universal humanism, making all peoples equal under Roman law regardless of creed? Or shall it extend its diplomatic network to make Rome the indispensable arbiter of all nations, an empire without end, bound not by force but by necessity?

modifiers.name: Universitas Romana
modifiers.text: The Roman university system has achieved something unprecedented: a truly universal standard of learning and governance. Roman humanism teaches that all peoples are equal before the law, though this tolerance means less zeal for religious conversion.

modifiers.name: Imperium Sine Fine
modifiers.text: Empire without end: the ancient prophecy is fulfilled, but through diplomacy rather than conquest. Rome is the indispensable nation, the arbiter of all disputes, the center of all alliances. The price of this diplomatic supremacy is a dilution of direct royal authority.

buildings.name: Castra Aeterna
buildings.text: The eternal legionary fortress: a permanent military installation built to Roman engineering standards, garrisoned by professional soldiers who live and die on the frontier. These fortresses project Roman power across vast distances.

buildings.name: Forum Universale
buildings.text: A grand civic center combining marketplace, library, and academy in the Roman tradition. Here merchants trade under Roman law while scholars study in Roman universities, creating a hub of civilization that draws the world to Rome.

list.name: Senatus Romanus Renovatus
list.text: On Pentecost 1144, after the death of Pope Innocent II, the Roman populace under Giordano Pierleoni proclaimed the renovatio senatus, electing fifty-six senators from the Capitoline to administer the city in defiance of papal temporal rule. The Lombard reformer Arnold of Brescia became the commune's intellectual leader and drove Pope Eugene III into exile in 1146 before his hanging in 1155. Versions of the senatorial commune persisted into the late medieval period, anchoring civic-aristocratic government against the cardinals.

list.name: Curia Romana
list.text: Created by Pope Urban II (r. 1088-1099) on the model of Cluniac monastic regulations and the Capetian royal council, the Roman Curia became Latin Christendom's most sophisticated administrative court. The Sacred College of Cardinals, meeting in regular consistories, served as the popes' standing council; cancellaria, dataria, and signatura departments were each headed by a cardinal. Bolognese-trained canon lawyers like Hostiensis turned the Curia into a continental clearing-house for ecclesiastical and political affairs.

list.name: Camera Apostolica
list.text: The papal treasury, headed by the Camerlengo of the Holy Roman Church. The office of camerarius was instituted by Pope Urban II and by the mid-12th century was a regular member of the Curia. After Innocent III (1198-1216) the regular assessment of crusade taxes built Latin Christendom's first cross-border revenue system, and the Camera drove the 13th-century shift from payments-in-kind to coined money across Mediterranean Europe.

list.name: Corpus Iuris Civilis
list.text: The rediscovery and teaching of Justinian's sixth-century legal compilation began at Bologna in the 1080s when Countess Matilda of Canossa invited the jurist Irnerius (the lucerna iuris) to lecture on the Digest. His school of glossators founded what became the University of Bologna in 1088, and the resulting ius commune fused Roman and canon law into the shared legal grammar of Latin Europe, replacing local feudal custom across the merchant cities of the peninsula.

list.name: Sacra Rota Romana
list.text: The apostolic court of appeals, emerged from the Audientia Sacri Palatii of the 12th-century Curia and formalised on 16 September 1331 by Pope John XXII's constitution Ratio iuris. Operating first from Avignon and later from the Apostolic Palace, its panel of auditores rotae became the supreme appellate court of Latin Christendom for both ecclesiastical and civil cases. It is the oldest continuously functioning court in Europe.

list.name: Banco di Santo Spirito
list.text: Founded by Pope Paul V on 13 December 1605 in the Palazzo del Banco built under Leo X on the Via dei Banchi, the Bank of the Holy Spirit was the first central bank in Europe to operate above the city-state level. Subordinate to the Archhospital of Santo Spirito (founded 1201), it was the first issuer of paper money in 1786 under Pius VI and remained the principal source of credit for ecclesiastical and commercial construction across the papal states for nearly four centuries.

list.name: Pontifex Maximus
list.text: The title of chief high priest of the Roman state religion, held by Augustus and his successors until Gratian relinquished it in 383 to Bishop Damasus of Rome. Latent through most of the medieval papacy, the title was revived in the fifteenth century by humanist popes (Nicholas V, Pius II, and above all Julius II) as a deliberate programme representing the Roman pontiff as heir to the imperial dignity of the Caesars and fusing classical antiquity with the militant Church.
